source: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
summary: MOSS anchors self-rewriting to production-failure evidence batches and delegates code modification to a pluggable coding-agent CLI. On OpenClaw it lifted mean grader score from 0.25 to 0.61 in one cycle without human intervention.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — conceptually interesting (failure-driven improvement) but falls squarely in the red-flag category: source-level self-evolution with no human gate, which conflicts with AgentForge's explicit human-approval checkpoints.

source: Andrej Karpathy: Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering (Sequoia AI Ascent 2026)
summary: Karpathy declares 'vibe coding' passé and coins 'agentic engineering' (Software 3.0): prompts + context + agents + tools + memory + verification as the new programming substrate. Joined Anthropic pretraining team May 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — conceptual framing, not an actionable technique. AgentForge already operates in this paradigm (explicit state machine, CLI agents, artifact-first).

source: DeerFlow 2.0 by ByteDance — Open-Source SuperAgent Harness
summary: Sub-agent orchestrator that decomposes goals into parallel sandboxed subtasks; primary orchestrator plans, delegates, monitors, synthesizes. Parallel sub-agents share memory but remain isolated.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — disciplined parallel sub-agent synthesis is interesting, but AgentForge deliberately chose sequential determinism over parallel execution. No prerequisite has changed. Maps to rejected candidates from prior triage.

source: LangChain and LangGraph v1.0 release + Deep Agents architecture
summary: LangGraph 1.0 is fully backward-compatible; Deep Agents launch adds built-in planning, filesystem, and sub-agent generation. LangChain OSS Skills released for agent framework expertise.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a custom CLI subprocess model (not LangChain/LangGraph). The 'Deep Agents' parallel roughly matches what AgentForge already does. Nothing actionable.

source: State of AI Agent Memory 2026 — episodic memory position paper
summary: Position paper argues episodic memory (reflection + consolidation into compact reusable representations) is the missing piece for long-term LLM agents. Three-tier architecture: in-context, semantic, episodic.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — but already covered: HID-188 tracks 'inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts'. No new angle not already scoped there.

source: Self-Improving AI Agents: Reflection Loop patterns (generate→critique→revise) 2026
summary: Production pattern: Actor generates, Evaluator scores, Self-Reflection module writes lesson into episodic memory. Includes single-model and multi-agent reflection variants (Skeptic/Logician/Creative personas).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the adversarial critique variant maps to HID-93 (adversarial plan critique before AwaitingPlanApproval). The single-model reflection loop partially maps to the existing PlanRevision cycle.

source: Agent Observability & Audit Trails in 2026 — Enterprise patterns
summary: OTel-first audit trails capturing tool calls, reasoning chains, state transitions, memory reads/writes. Distinction: traces (engineer debugging) vs audit trails (compliance/explainability). OpenTelemetry now table stakes.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — overlaps with HID-163 (per-run token cost and stage latency telemetry). The structured audit trail / OTel dimension is slightly broader but the same capability theme; adding a separate issue would fragment the work.

summary: Survey from bounded self-refinement to autonomous research loops; classifies self-improvement into prompt-level, skill-level, and source-level with safety analysis.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — theoretical survey. Red-flag category (RL training loops, self-modification). No concrete implementable gap identified for AgentForge within 1-2 agent runs.

source: AutoGen 0.4 / Microsoft Agent Framework and CrewAI 1.0 updates
summary: AutoGen 0.4 in maintenance mode; Microsoft redirects new projects to Microsoft Agent Framework. CrewAI 1.0 stable with Flows; AMP enterprise extensions. LangGraph surpassed CrewAI in GitHub stars.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — framework-level churn. AgentForge's CLI subprocess model is framework-agnostic; it runs claude/codex binaries directly and is unaffected by these version milestones.

source: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: Workshop collecting research on AI systems that modify their own learning processes or capabilities; covers prompt-level, skill-level, architecture-level self-modification.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — academic workshop; same red-flag themes as above. No concrete pattern extractable for AgentForge in 1-2 runs.
